items.title: Where do the two strategies' conflict counts actually diverge?
items.description: Using the exact simulation from L3 (seed 42, 6 hot files, one file touched per day by trunk and by the feature work), drag the sprint length and watch how trunk-based and gitflow's total conflict counts compare. At 10 days, this reproduces L3's verified 0-vs-4 reading exactly.
items.compute: function mulberry32(seed) { return function () { seed |= 0; seed = (seed + 0x6d2b79f5) | 0; let t = Math.imul(seed ^ (seed >>> 15), 1 | seed); t = (t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), 61 | t)) ^ t; return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296; }; } const hotFiles = ['auth.js', 'router.js', 'db.js', 'utils.js', 'api.js', 'types.js']; function pickFile(rand) { return hotFiles[Math.floor(rand() * hotFiles.length)]; } function simulateTrunkBased(rand, days) { let c = 0; for (let d = 0; d < days; d++) { const t = pickFile(rand); const b = pickFile(rand); if (t === b) c++; } return c; } function simulateGitflow(rand, days) { const t = new Set(); const b = new Set(); for (let d = 0; d < days; d++) { t.add(pickFile(rand)); b.add(pickFile(rand)); } let c = 0; for (const f of b) if (t.has(f)) c++; return c; } const r1 = mulberry32(42); const r2 = mulberry32(42); return { trunkConflicts: simulateTrunkBased(r1, params.sprintDays), gitflowConflicts: simulateGitflow(r2, params.sprintDays) };
